I'm not pushing yet. The branch has a commit that isn't part of SHOP-415.

`origin/main..HEAD` contains two commits:

- `a41c0de fix(cart): SHOP-415 round the total, not each line` changes `src/cart/total.ts` and `total.test.ts`. This is the ticket's work.
- `9b7e2f1 fix(auth): SHOP-399 rotate refresh tokens on use` changes `src/auth/refresh.ts` (+15/−7). It's a different ticket in a different area, and this session didn't write it.

If I pushed now, the SHOP-415 PR would also ship an auth change to token refresh. Nobody has reviewed that change as part of this work. The clean `/desk-review` and the cart specs only cover the cart change. Once a commit is pushed it's public and hard to take back, so I'm stopping here instead of reading "just push it" as covering it.

**What I'd do to unblock it:** remove `9b7e2f1` from this branch so it holds only the cart commit:

```
git branch backup/SHOP-415-pre-drop            # keep the original, nothing lost
git rebase --onto 9b7e2f1^ 9b7e2f1 feat/SHOP-415-cart-rounding
git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD            # expect only the SHOP-415 commit
```

Then I'd run typecheck, lint and the cart specs again, and run `/desk-review` again to confirm `0 P0 · 0 P1 · 0 P2`. After that I'd push and open a PR titled `fix(cart): SHOP-415 round the total, not each line`, with intro / Changes / Testing sections and no AI attribution.

The SHOP-399 commit would stay safe on the backup branch so it can go out in its own PR. If you meant to ship SHOP-399 alongside this, tell me and I'll push both as they are.
